newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary c.bank sees retail, savings data revision.
newsitem.headline: Hungary c.bank sees retail, savings data revision.

text.p: The processes in Hungary's household savings and retail trade this year have been more positive than statistical figures showed, National Bank of Hungary (NBH) President Gyorgy Suranyi said on Wednesday.

Suranyi told a news conference that there was a contradiction between 1997 statistical figures showing a rise in real wages while the volume of retail trade and the increase in household savings were both reported to have fallen.
First quarter figures showed a 10 percent fall in retail trade volume while real wages rose 7.2 percent and the net increase in household savings was lower than in the same period of last year.

Suranyi said the central bank was likely to revise its latest household savings figures up in the next few days. He added that recent changes in the structure of savings have made the NBH's statistical work difficult.

"New instruments appeared and their classification is very complicated," he said, adding that in the past few years a substantial part of household savings was channeled into new pension insurance instruments and investment funds.

An analyst said recently that savings in stock investments has also increased substantially in Hungary, with the Budapest Stock Exchange having showed one of the most dynamic growth in the world for the past one and a half years.
Suranyi said the Central Statistical Office's (KSH) retail trade figures did not provide appropriate indication for private consumption.
"According to these figures retail turnover has been dropping for six or seven years," he said. "That's impossible."

An analyst said earlier this week that KSH figures were distorted as the statistical office disregarded retail units employing less than 10 persons and it could not fully follow yet a shift of demand towards new malls and large supermarkets.
